## 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 (id: eng-2ch-p8-v1)

Hear and Heart
--------------

In this step, hear 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the previous story, King Solomon finished building and furnishing the temple. While the previous story showed all of the new items and parts of the temple, this story focuses more on items that King Solomon still needs to bring to the temple and how the Israelites move these items to the temple. This is the same story as the story in 1 Kings 8:1–11, but with a few different details.

Stop here and do this activity as a group: If you have already translated 1 Kings 8:1–11, listen to your translation of that passage. Pause this audio here.

Stop here as a group and review the photo of King Solomon's temple. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon cannot complete the temple fully until the ark of the covenant, the Tent of Meeting, and any furnishings the priests use in the Tent of Meeting are in the temple. King Solomon asks the elders and heads or chiefs of the Israelite tribes to gather together and to join the people who will bring the ark of the covenant, the Tent of Meeting, and the furnishings to the temple. You will remember that the Tent of Meeting is the temporary tent that the Israelites used to meet with Yahweh before Solomon built the temple.

Stop here as a group and look at a photo of the ark of the covenant. Pause this audio here.

Stop and look at a photo or illustration of the Tent of Meeting and furnishings. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think of a time when you were close to completing a task, but you had to wait for someone else to come or something else to happen before you could finish. How did you feel? Discuss this question with the group. Pause this audio here.

It is important to pay attention to the people that King Solomon gathers together for this process. The term "elders" likely refers to the older men who oversee the people of Israel, and "heads" or "chiefs" likely refers to the men who are in charge of leading their households and different tribes. It is possible that these are all the same leaders, but it is also possible that there are different sets of leaders who help look after the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think about the types of leadership in your community. Discuss as a group the different kinds of leaders and who takes care of the different groups of people in your community. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon wants the elders to walk with the people who will carry the ark, the Tent of Meeting, and the furnishings from Zion to King Solomon's location north of Zion. People sometimes use Zion as another name for Jerusalem or the City of David. It is likely that the storyteller uses Zion here to show that King Solomon is moving the ark from King David's Jerusalem to the new location of the temple in a different place.

It is also important to notice the time of year when King Solomon starts this process. The storyteller says that King Solomon chooses the seventh month. The seventh month means the seventh month when Solomon finished the temple, and not the seventh month in the time that the storyteller wrote the story. The seventh month is likely the same as mid\-September or October today.

At this time of year, the Israelites celebrated a feast called the Festival of Tabernacles. The Festival of Tabernacles was likely a perfect time for King Solomon because the festival celebrates when the Israelites left Egypt and had to live in temporary shelters. The festival also celebrates how Yahweh gave the Israelites a permanent place to live after the Israelites wandered for years in the desert. The Festival of Tabernacles is a pilgrimage feast, which means that the tribes of Israel travel to Jerusalem for this festival. This also means that the elders, chiefs, and men of Israel are in Jerusalem at the time that King Solomon asks for them to come to the temple. It is likely that King Solomon finished the temple and then waited for this festival so that the people who were allowed to transport the ark of the covenant, the Tent of Meeting, and the furnishings could easily bring everything to the new temple. This also means that the people of Israel could all be at the temple together to see the dedication.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think of celebrations or festivals you have in your community that help you remember specific days or events. How do you celebrate? Pause this audio here.

Only men from the tribe of Levi can carry the pieces from Zion to the new temple. The priests, who are from the tribe of Levi, are the only people Yahweh has allowed to carry the ark of the covenant. The Levites who are not priests are allowed to carry the Tent of Meeting and the furnishings from the Tent of Meeting. It is likely that King Solomon and the people of Israel traveled with the priests and other Levites. It is also likely that King Solomon and the people of Israel sacrificed cattle and sheep during the journey, as well as at the temple. The storyteller says that the people sacrificed so many cattle and sheep that people could not keep count of them all.

Stop here and look at pictures of cattle and sheep. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at a picture of what a priest looked like and the clothing they wore. Pause this audio here.

When the priests arrive at the temple, the priests carry the ark of the covenant into the temple's inner room, called the Most Holy Place. It is important to remember that there are two rooms within the building where the priests perform their priestly duties. The Holy Place is a room or space where all priests can go. Only the high priest can go into the Most Holy Place, which some people call the Inner Sanctuary.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a photo or diagram of the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what places or areas can only certain people go into? Pause this audio here.

The priests place the ark of the covenant under the wings of two cherubim angels that people made from olive wood and covered in gold. The cherubim are probably a larger version of the smaller cherubim that used to rest on the corners of the ark. The larger cherubim spread their wings over the entire ark and the carrying poles to show that this is Yahweh's resting place. The carrying poles for the ark are so long that a priest can see the poles as they are standing in the Holy Place, but not outside the Holy Place. This likely means that the poles press into the curtain that separates the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place. The storyteller says that the poles are still attached to the ark, but this likely means that the poles are there at the time the storyteller writes this. It is likely that the storyteller shares this section to help the reader visualize the new space of the temple.

Stop here and look at an illustration of cherubim. Also, look at an illustration of what the cherubim looked like in Solomon's temple. Pause this audio here.

It is important to remember that Moses put two tablets in the ark of the covenant. These flat stones represent the covenant that Yahweh made with the Israelites on Mount Horeb, also known as Mount Sinai. The storyteller says that these two tablets, which show God's covenant with Israel after they were free from Egypt, are the only items inside the ark of the covenant.

Stop here and look at an illustration of the two tablets that Moses put into the ark of the covenant. Pause this audio here.

After the priests leave the ark of the covenant in the Most Holy Place, the storyteller shares a new part of the story. The storyteller talks more about the Levites in this passage than in the 1 Kings story. It is likely that the storyteller wants to make sure that the listener knows that there are more people than just priests participating in the temple dedication.

Stop here and discuss as a group: The storyteller chose to include more information on the Levites in this passage than in the 1 Kings passage. Why might you sometimes retell a story and include different details at different times? Pause this audio here.

All of the priests who were at the temple and who were participating in this process needed to be spiritually clean. Yahweh gave the priests certain rituals to do in order to be ready to serve Yahweh. All priests would pray and wash their hands in the holy water in the basin. This means that all of the priests purified themselves regardless of whose turn it was, so they would be ready to serve. Because there are probably more priests and Levites than they need at one time, the priests and Levites take turns serving in the temple. Also, there are different tasks that the Levites perform.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How do you prepare for important work that you have to do? What rituals or routines do you perform in order to prepare? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: In your culture, what do priests do to prepare to serve or do their job? How do people prepare themselves to worship God? Pause this audio here.

In this next part, the storyteller specifically shares about the groups of Levites who make music. The Levite musicians Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their relatives stand on the east side of the altar.

Asaph is a Levite who has served in Jerusalem, while Heman and Jeduthun are Levites who served in the tabernacle in Gibeon. All of the Levitical singers and musicians are wearing fine linen. This is important because Yahweh told them to wear this to show they are purified and prepared to serve. All of the musicians play cymbals, harps, and lyres. Cymbals are two small, metal instruments that a person can hold and strike together with one hand. Both harps and lyres are stringed instruments that a person can pluck with their fingers. The storyteller also says that 120 priests join the other Levitical musicians and play trumpets. A trumpet is a long and slender instrument that is often silver or bronze. A person plays a trumpet by blowing into the mouthpiece to make sounds or music. When the singers sing along with the trumpets, the people hear such a perfect song that it sounds like the singers and musicians are making one unified sound to Yahweh!

Stop here and look at photos of cymbals, a harp, a lyre, a trumpet, and fine linen. Pause this audio here.

While the musicians play, the singers sing about Yahweh. The singers sing, "He is good. His steadfast love continues forever." The Israelites often sing this in worship to remind each other of all that Yahweh has done for them. This phrase is a phrase that the people of Israel use often to worship Yahweh and to remind each other of all that Yahweh has done for the people.

Stop here and discuss as a group: What phrases do you say or sing in your community that you often repeat? What religious phrases or songs do people repeat? Pause this audio here.

The storyteller then returns to a retelling of the similar passage in 1 Kings 8:1–11\.

Then, a cloud fills the temple. The cloud is the presence and glory of Yahweh, and the cloud is so thick that the priests cannot do their priestly duties. It is important to remember that when Moses finished building the Tent of Meeting, a cloud covered the tent and Yahweh's glory filled the space. The storyteller likely uses this same description to show that Yahweh's presence is now in the new temple and that Yahweh is blessing the temple.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Think of a time when a room was so full that you could not go in. This could be a time when there were too many people in a room, when a room was too hot, or even when a room was filled with smoke. Imagine how it felt, and then discuss the cloud that filled the temple. Discuss how this might have felt and how you would feel.

Defining the Scenes
-------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has six scenes.

**In the first scene:** King Solomon summons the elders and chiefs of the people of Israel.

**In the second scene:** The priests bring the ark of the covenant to the temple, and the Levites bring the Tent of Meeting and furnishings to the temple.

**In the third scene:** The people of Israel sacrifice cattle and sheep.

**In the fourth scene:** The priests bring the ark of the covenant into the Most Holy Place.

**In the fifth scene:** The priests purify themselves.

**In the sixth scene:** The priests leave the Holy Place, and the priests sing as Yahweh's presence fills the temple.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* Elders and chiefs of the people of Israel
* Priests who carry the ark of the covenant
* Levites who carry the Tent of Meeting and furnishings
* People of Israel
* Priests who play the trumpets
* Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun
* And the Levites who are singers and musicians, including family members of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, King Solomon summons the elders and chiefs of the people of Israel. This is important because the leaders and chiefs are in charge of looking after the people and communicating King Solomon's commands to the people. Remember that the term "elders" likely refers to the older men who oversee the people of Israel, and "heads" or "chiefs" likely means the men who are in charge of leading their household and different tribes.

Stop here and discuss as a group: What words or phrases do you use in your culture for leaders or chiefs? How can you best translate this? Pause this audio here.

In the first scene, King Solomon has just finished building the temple. King Solomon wants the priests to bring the ark of the covenant and the Levites to bring the Tent of Meeting and furnishings from Zion to the temple near where King Solomon lives. Although the storyteller does not say this specifically, the people of Israel are gathering in Jerusalem for the Festival of Tabernacles and can travel easily to King Solomon. King Solomon likely knows that the temple is not finished until the priests and Levites bring these items. King Solomon also likely chooses the Festival of Tabernacles in the seventh month as a time to do this because the festival requires all people of Israel to travel to Jerusalem.

Stop here as a group and review the picture of King Solomon's temple. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: In this passage, a festival is a gathering where people celebrate an event or special occasion. In your language, how would you translate "festival"? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, once the elders and leaders gather together with Solomon, the priests and Levites prepare to go to the temple. The priests carry the ark of the covenant with the poles. The other Levites carry the Tent of Meeting and the other furnishings from the Tent of Meeting. The elders and chiefs travel with the priests and Levites who transport all that King Solomon has asked for.

Stop here as a group and look at a photo of the ark of the covenant, the Tent of Meeting, and the furnishings. Pause this audio here.

It is important to remember that Yahweh said that the priests are the only ones who can carry or touch the poles of the ark. It is also important that only the other Levites carry the Tent of Meeting and furnishings, because Yahweh gave the Levites the duty to care for the temple.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Think about the roles and duties in your culture that only certain people can perform. What are examples of these types or roles and duties? How can you use this information to talk about the Levites in this passage? Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, the priests, Levites and other leaders arrive at the temple and see King Solomon sacrificing cattle and sheep. It is possible King Solomon walked ahead of the ark and arrived at the temple first. The people of Israel are sacrificing so many cattle and sheep that it is impossible to count all of the sacrifices! Solomon and the people dedicate the temple to Yahweh and honor Yahweh with these sacrifices.

Stop here and look at pictures of cattle and sheep. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: In your culture, what word could you use for sacrifices, and how could you explain the amount of sacrifices? How could you talk about something that no one can count because there are so many of them, such as dust or grains of sand? Pause this audio here.

In the fourth scene, the priests carry the ark of the covenant to the place where Yahweh always wanted it to be. This is often known as its proper place, the Inner Sanctuary, or the Most Holy Place. Only the priests are able to enter any of these spaces. The priests place the ark of the covenant under the outspread cherubim wings, and the priests leave the poles in the ark and then leave.

Stop here and look at a photo or illustration of cherubim. Also, look at a photo or illustration of what the cherubim looked like in Solomon's temple. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Look again at the cherubim. Discuss as a group how you can describe the cherubim and how you can show the difference between a real angel and the carved angel. Pause this audio here.

In the fifth scene, the priests have all made themselves pure by making sure they are spiritually clean. The Levites are singing and playing instruments. Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun are with their male sons and male relatives as they all sing and play the cymbals, harps, and lyres. One hundred and twenty priests join the other Levitical musicians, and the priests play the trumpets. The singers, musicians, and priests who play the trumpets join together to make music and offer up one unified sound to worship Yahweh. The singers sing these words about Yahweh: "He is good. His steadfast love continues forever."

Stop here and look at a photo of cymbals, a harp, a lyre, a trumpet, and fine linen. Pause this audio here.

In the sixth scene, a cloud fills the temple as the priests and Levites leave the Holy Place. The priests and Levites sing and play music. The cloud is Yahweh's presence and glory. The cloud is so thick that the priests cannot carry out their priestly duties, and the priests have to leave the sanctuary. Yahweh often showed that Yahweh was in a space when Yahweh filled that space with a cloud or bright light. The cloud is important because it shows that Yahweh now fills the temple and rests in the place that King Solomon built to honor Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you describe the cloud? In your culture, how do you show that something like a cloud represents a person? Think about objects in your culture that represent a person when you cannot see the person. For instance, a throne or crown can represent a king's power. Discuss how you can describe Yahweh in the cloud. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text
------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has six scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* Elders and chiefs of the people of Israel
* Priests who carry the ark of the covenant
* Levites who carry the Tent of Meeting and furnishings
* People of Israel
* Priests who play the trumpets
* Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun
* And Levitical singers and musicians, including family members of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

After King Solomon finishes building the temple, King Solomon asks the elders and chiefs of the people of Israel to meet Solomon in Jerusalem so the people can celebrate together as the priests carry the ark of the covenant into the temple. King Solomon asks the priests to carry the ark of the covenant with its poles and the other Levites to carry the Tent of Meeting and its furnishings to the new temple.

All of the people of Israel are in Jerusalem for the Festival of Tabernacles, including the priests, the Levites, and the elders and chiefs whom King Solomon had asked to come.

Pause the drama. Ask the people playing priests, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* What an honor to carry the ark to the temple! or
* We must be careful! or
* We must not forget anything!

> Continue the drama.
> 
> Once the elders and all leaders gather together with Solomon, the priests and Levites go to the new temple. The priests walk and carry the ark of the covenant, and the other Levites also walk and carry the Tent of Meeting and its furnishings. King Solomon, the elders, the other chiefs of the tribes of Israel, and the Israelites travel to the temple as well.

Pause the drama. Ask the people playing the other Levites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* We must carry everything carefully for Yahweh; or
* I am very tired from walking and carrying everything! or
* I wonder what the temple will look like!

> Continue the drama.
> 
> When all of the elders, leaders, priests, and other Levites reach King Solomon, they see the rest of the people of Israel. The people of Israel are sacrificing so many cattle and sheep for Yahweh that it is impossible to count all of the sacrifices!

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing King Solomon, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* Finally, everyone has arrived! or
* I can now dedicate the temple properly! or
* Surely Yahweh will be pleased with all of these sacrifices!

Ask the people playing the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* There cannot possibly be any more animals left! or
* I wonder what Yahweh thinks about all of this! or
* I feel excited to have the temple completed!

> Continue the drama.

The priests then carry the ark of the covenant into the Most Holy Place. The priests place the ark of the covenant, with the two stone tablets that Moses put into the ark, under the cherubim that will cover the ark of the covenant and the poles.

Ask the people playing the priests, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* I am so relieved that we brought the ark here safely! or
* I am in awe of the cherubim! or
* I must make sure the curtain is closed.

> Continue the drama.

The priests leave the Holy Place. The priests have all made themselves holy by making sure they are spiritually clean. The priests have washed their hands in the water basin and performed other priestly rituals. The Levites who are musicians are playing the cymbals, harps, and lyres. Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, as well as their sons and family, play instruments on the east side of the altar. One hundred and twenty priests join in and play trumpets with the musicians. As the Levites and priests play, the singers join in perfectly to worship Yahweh by singing, "He is good. His love continues forever."

Ask the people playing Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* I love to play instruments for Yahweh! or
* I hope this pleases Yahweh! or
* I feel so honored to be here!

Ask the people playing priests with trumpets, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* We must play loudly for everyone to hear! or
* Wow, we blend perfectly with the voices! or
* I feel thankful to Yahweh!

> Continue the drama.
> 
> Then, a cloud fills the entire temple. The cloud is Yahweh's presence, and Yahweh shows that Yahweh is pleased with the temple. The cloud is so thick that the priests cannot enter the temple to perform their priestly duties. Yahweh's presence fills the temple, and all of the people can see that Yahweh is pleased and that Yahweh is now in the temple.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* King Solomon has truly honored and obeyed me! or
* Everything looks exactly like I wanted it to; or
* I love King Solomon and the people of Israel!

Ask the people playing the priests, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* How can we perform our duties in the temple if we cannot get in? or
* I can feel Yahweh's presence here! or
* We must help the people of Israel understand what is happening.

Filling the Gaps
----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 5:2–14 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, King Solomon summons the elders and chiefs of the people of Israel. The elders led the entire population of the people of Israel. The chiefs are leaders of different groups or tribes of people. King Solomon chooses to do this during the time of the Festival of Tabernacles. You will remember that the people of Israel celebrated the Festival of Tabernacles to remember when Yahweh provided the people with shelter after they left Egypt.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **chiefs**, **elders**, and the **Festival of Tabernacles.** Remember that the storyteller does not use the title of the Festival of Tabernacles in this story. Look up elders, **king**, **Israel**, and Festival of Tabernacles in the Master Glossary for more information.

King Solomon wants the **priests** and other Levites to bring the **ark of the covenant**, the Tent of Meeting, also known as the **tabernacle**, and the "**holy**" or special tent furnishings from their location in Jerusalem, also called Zion, north to where King Solomon has built the **temple**. Remember that the priests and Levites were both part of the tribe of Levi. Priests offered sacrifices to Yahweh for the people of Israel. Other Levites served the temple in other ways, such as playing music, singing, and doing other tasks for the temple. The ark of the covenant was the oblong chest that people had made of wood and covered in gold. The presence of Yahweh rested on top of the ark on the atonement seat. The tabernacle was the movable tent where Yahweh's presence rested. The temple became the permanent building for Yahweh's presence and the ark of the covenant. Use the same words or phrases for holy, priests, ark of the covenant, tabernacle, and temple as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, priest, ark of the covenant, tabernacle, and temple, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here as a group and look at a photo or diagram of the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **Zion** and **Levites**. Look up Levite and Zion in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated these words in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The people of Israel **sacrifice** so many cattle and sheep that no one can keep count of the amount of animals. Cattle refers to any kind of cow, ox, or bull. Use the same word or phrase for sacrificing as you used in previous passages. For more information on sacrifice, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priests take the ark of the covenant through the **Inner Sanctuary** into the **Most Holy Place**. The priests place the ark of the covenant under the **cherubim** with wings that stretch over the entire length of the ark and the carrying poles. The carrying poles were so long that when the priests stood in the Holy Place, the priests could see the poles pressing into the curtain from the Most Holy Place. Use the same words or phrases for sanctuary, Most Holy Place, and cherubim as you used in previous passages. For more information on sanctuary, Most Holy Place, and cherubim, refer to the Master Glossary.

After the priests leave the **Holy Place** or sanctuary, Levite musicians are standing to the east of the **altar**. The priests have **consecrated** or made themselves holy by cleaning their bodies and committing themselves to Yahweh. Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, along with their sons and families, play the cymbals, harps, and lyres while they wear fine linen clothing. One hundred and twenty priests join in by playing trumpets. Cymbals are two small, metal instruments that a person can hold and strike together with one hand. Both harps and lyres are stringed instruments that a person can pluck with their fingers. Trumpets are metal instruments with a mouthpiece, slender body, and a flared part at the bottom where the sound escapes. As the musicians play, the singers **praise** Yahweh and sing the words, "He is good. His **steadfast love** continues forever." For more information on Holy Place, altar, consecrate, praise, and steadfast love, refer to the Master Glossary.

Then, a cloud fills the temple, and **Yahweh's** presence and glory enters into the temple to stay and rest there. The cloud is so thick that the priests cannot enter to perform their priestly duties in the temple. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you have used previously, and refer to the Master Glossary for more information about Yahweh.

Stop here as a team and look and images of linen, cymbals, harps, lyres, and trumpets, if needed. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **cloud**, **linen**, **cymbals**, **harps**, **lyres**, **trumpets**, and **glory**. Look up glory in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated these words in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there.

## 2 Chronicles 6:1–11 (id: eng-2ch-p9-v1)

Hear and Heart
--------------

In this step, hear \[2 Chronicles 6:1–11]{.mark} and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of \[2 Chronicles 6:1–11]{.mark} three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of \[2 Chronicles 6:1–11]{.mark} in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the previous passage, Yahweh saw all that King Solomon and the people of Israel did. When the priests placed the ark of the covenant in the Most Holy Place, Yahweh responded when he filled the temple with a thick cloud. In this passage, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh in a prayer and then addresses the people of Israel in response to Yahweh's presence in the temple.

Stop here and review the photo of King Solomon's temple. Pause this audio here.

This passage is almost exactly the same as 1 Kings 8:12–21 that you may have translated previously.

Stop here and do this activity as a group: If you have already translated 1 Kings 8:12–21, listen to your translation of that passage. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon begins his prayer when Solomon talks about what Yahweh has previously said. In the book of Leviticus, Yahweh spoke to Moses and told Moses not to allow Moses' brother Aaron to go into the Most Holy Place. Yahweh also said that Yahweh would come in a dark cloud in the Holy Place over the ark of the covenant. This was a sign that Yahweh was pleased and was present in the tabernacle. When Yahweh shows up in a dark and thick cloud this time, Yahweh does the same thing as Yahweh did in the time of Moses. King Solomon realizes this and tells Yahweh that King Solomon has built a magnificent temple for Yahweh to live in forever.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Remember that the people of Israel likely knew the story of Moses and Yahweh's presence in the tabernacle. How do you think the people felt when they saw this happen? How would you feel if you saw this with your own eyes instead of only hearing about it? Pause this audio here.

After King Solomon prays to Yahweh, King Solomon then turns away from the temple and faces the assembly, or the group of the people of Israel. Assemblies are large groups of people who gather together for a common reason. King Solomon then blesses the people. Again, King Solomon does the same act that Moses did at the tabernacle. King Solomon sees all that has happened, and King Solomon honors Yahweh and then speaks Yahweh's blessings over the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think about the most important or famous person in your country or beyond. This could be a king or a leader. How does this person bless people in your culture? How would you feel if this person recognized you and spoke kind words to you? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon begins his blessing and speech by praising Yahweh, the God of Israel. The title of "God of Israel" reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is Israel's God, whom the people should worship. \[King Solomon says he praises Yahweh because Yahweh has fulfilled Yahweh's promises through Yahweh's hands, or Yahweh's power.]{.mark} Yahweh fulfilled his promise to Solomon's father, King David, that Solomon would be king and build the temple. King Solomon likely wants to remind the people that Yahweh is faithful and trustworthy.

In the next section, King Solomon speaks words that Yahweh has already spoken. These words are not King Solomon's interpretation of Yahweh's words. King Solomon quotes Yahweh when Solomon says these words: "Since the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city in any tribe of Israel for people to build a temple in so that my name might be there, nor have I chosen anyone to be ruler over my people Israel. But now I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to rule my people Israel." Yahweh means that people will honor and respect Yahweh's name, which is Yahweh himself, and the people will not worship other names in Jerusalem.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Refer back to the 1 Kings 8:12–21 translation. What is different about this section? In your culture, how often do people tell the same stories but include different true details? Pause this audio here.

In this part of the passage, King Solomon likely shares what Yahweh said to King David, to explain why King David did not build the temple sooner. Yahweh wanted King David to rule over the people of Israel, but Yahweh did not give King David permission or instructions to build a temple.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Imagine that you are King David. How would you feel if you were king and you wanted to build a temple, but Yahweh would not let you? Describe your feelings and thoughts. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: In your culture, who do people allow to build or create holy places like temples? Who chooses when it is the right time or place to make these holy places? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then quotes Yahweh again to remind the people of Israel why King Solomon built the temple. Yahweh did not let King David build the temple, even though Yahweh loved King David and King David wanted to build the temple to honor Yahweh's name. However, Yahweh did have a plan. Yahweh told King David that King David's son, King Solomon, would build the temple. Yahweh makes sure that King David understands the word "son" when he says that David's "flesh and blood" would be the one to build the temple. When Solomon repeats Yahweh's words, King Solomon reminds the people of Israel that Yahweh is faithful and is in control of all things, including time.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think of a time when you thought someone would choose you for a special role, but the person chose someone else. Share with the group how you felt. Pause this audio here.

After King Solomon reminds the people of what Yahweh said, King Solomon then confirms that what Yahweh said has happened. Yahweh has kept all of Yahweh's promises. Solomon is king and has built the temple for Yahweh, just as Yahweh promised. Again, King Solomon says that he has built the temple for "Yahweh, God of Israel."

Stop here and look at a picture of a throne. Pause this audio here.

To finish King Solomon's reminder to the people, King Solomon explains that King Solomon has built a place for the ark of the covenant. In the ark are the stone tablets. These tablets are a reminder of Yahweh's covenant with the people of Israel after Yahweh led the people of Israel out of Egypt. King Solomon reminds the people of Israel that Yahweh made promises to their ancestors. Yahweh will keep those promises just like Yahweh kept his promises to David.

Stop here and look at a picture of the ark of the covenant. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at a picture of the stone tablets. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you pass information down through generations so that people will know what happened during their ancestors' lives? How do you keep a record of all that has happened?

Defining the Scenes
-------------------

Listen to an audio version of \[2 Chronicles 6:1–11]{.mark} in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

**In the first scene:** King Solomon faces the temple and speaks to Yahweh.

**In the second scene:** King Solomon turns around and blesses the people of Israel. King Solomon reminds the people of how Yahweh keeps his promises.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* People of Israel
* And King David

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, King Solomon is the only one who speaks. King Solomon speaks first to Yahweh and then to the people of Israel. King Solomon praises Yahweh, tells the story of what Yahweh has done, and reminds the people that Yahweh keeps Yahweh's promises.

In the first scene, King Solomon faces the temple and speaks to Yahweh. King Solomon reminds Yahweh, and anyone listening, that Yahweh previously said that Yahweh would live in a dark cloud. King Solomon is referring to another time when Yahweh spoke to Moses. King Solomon then offers the new temple to Yahweh so that Yahweh can have a place to live in forever. When King Solomon says he built the temple, King Solomon represents all of the people who helped build the temple; King Solomon did not build the temple by himself. The storyteller shows that King Solomon pays attention to Yahweh's previous words and shows that he knows what Yahweh is doing.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how will you translate this part so that people will understand that King Solomon's words are words that Yahweh has already said in earlier passages? How will you make it clear that Solomon is speaking about Yahweh, and Solomon is speaking directly to Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, King Solomon turns away from the temple and turns towards the people. Solomon speaks to the people of Israel. The storyteller says that the people are standing as an assembly or group, so King Solomon is likely talking to people who are actively listening to Solomon. King Solomon blessed the people.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what type or types of blessings do people speak over people? Think of examples of how people might speak words to people for comfort or to remind those people of how Yahweh blesses them. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon talks about both what Yahweh does now and what Yahweh has said and done in the past. King Solomon starts by praising "Yahweh, the God of Israel" for helping King Solomon do what Yahweh told King David with Yahweh's mouth that King Solomon would do. It is important to notice the small difference here from the parallel passage in 1 Kings 8:12–21\. King Solomon says here that Yahweh's "hands," not just Yahweh's "hand," kept Yahweh's promises. These mean the same thing. The storyteller does not mean that Yahweh's actual hands built the temple. But the storyteller likely means that Yahweh made it possible through Yahweh's power and strength for King Solomon and the people to complete the temple.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: When you tell a story in your language and culture, how do you show that something happens now and that something happened in the past? What words would you use to help someone understand when something happened? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how will you talk about the "hand, or strength, of Yahweh" in this passage? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Solomon uses the phrases "with his hand" and "with his mouth" to describe Yahweh's actions. How can you show Yahweh's actions in your language? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then talks about what Yahweh said to King David. After the people of Israel left Egypt, Yahweh did not give a specific place for anyone to build a temple, and Yahweh had not chosen anyone to rule. Yahweh did not choose any person to rule because Yahweh ruled the Israelites. However, eventually Yahweh did choose Jerusalem as the place where people would honor Yahweh's name. Yahweh also blessed King David and chose King David to rule over the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How can you show the difference between the way a person speaks their own words and the way a person quotes another person's words? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then explains that his father, King David, "had it in his heart" to build a temple for Yahweh. In the Hebrew language, people talk about the heart as the place where people think and feel. King David desired to build the temple to honor Yahweh's name. Again, King Solomon says, "Yahweh, God of Israel," and King Solomon is using two names to describe Yahweh.

King Solomon then tells the people that King Solomon's father, King David, wanted to build a temple for Yahweh. Then King Solomon again quotes Yahweh's words that Yahweh spoke to King David. Yahweh told King David that Yahweh was pleased that King David wanted to build a temple for Yahweh. However, Yahweh tells King David that King David will not be the one who builds the temple. Instead, Yahweh chose King Solomon, King David's own "flesh and blood," to build the temple for Yahweh. In this case, flesh and blood means King David's son, not King David's own skin and blood.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how do you show that someone is related to someone else? How can you translate phrases like "flesh and blood" so that people can understand what these ideas mean? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Why do you think King Solomon repeats Yahweh's promises? What are some reasons why it is helpful to repeat stories or phrases? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon finishes this prayer when Solomon makes it clear to the people that Yahweh has kept the promises that Yahweh made to King David. King Solomon now sits on Israel's throne and rules over the people of Israel. King Solomon has also built the temple for Yahweh and has placed the ark of the covenant in the temple. King Solomon also reminds the people that the covenant is in the ark of the covenant. The covenant refers to the tablets, which represent the covenant that Yahweh made with Moses and the people of Israel when Yahweh freed the people of Israel from Egypt.

Stop here and look at a picture of a throne. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at a picture of the ark of the covenant. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at a picture of the stone tablets. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

After Yahweh's presence fills the **temple**, **King** Solomon faces the temple and speaks to Yahweh. King Solomon says that Yahweh previously said that Yahweh would live in a dark **cloud**. King Solomon praises or **blesses** **Yahweh**, the **God** of **Israel**, and tells the people of Israel that Yahweh has fulfilled with Yahweh's hands what Yahweh told King Solomon's father, King David, with Yahweh's mouth. Use the same words or phrases for assembly, bless, Yahweh, God, and Israel as you used in previous passages. Look up Israel, praise, Yahweh, God, and bless in the Master Glossary for more information.

King Solomon says that King David had it in his **heart** to build a house for Yahweh. Yahweh told King David that Yahweh had not chosen any city in any **tribe** of Israel for anyone to build a temple. However, Yahweh did choose for King David to rule over the people of Israel. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about heart, and use the same words or phrases for heart and tribe as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said that King David's son, King David's own "flesh and blood," would build the temple.

Finally, King Solomon reminds the people of Israel that King Solomon placed the **ark of the covenant** in the temple. Use the same words or phrases for ark of the covenant and covenant as you used in previous passages. Look up ark of the covenant and covenant in the Master Glossary for more information.

Setting the Stage
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:12–21 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

This passage in 2 Chronicles is a parallel or similar passage to the passage in 1 Kings 8:22–30 that you previously translated. If you have already translated 1 Kings 8:22–30, stop here and review your translation of that passage.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, King Solomon continues to pray to Yahweh in front of the people of Israel. This passage contains two sections within King Solomon's prayers. In the first part of King Solomon's prayers, King Solomon praises Yahweh for how Yahweh has kept and fulfilled Yahweh's covenant or promise to King Solomon's father, King David. In the second part of this prayer, King Solomon asks that Yahweh listen to the Israelites' prayers.

As King Solomon continues to pray to Yahweh, King Solomon stands facing the bronze temple altar, with the people of Israel behind King Solomon. It is important to remember that this is the altar that is in front of the temple building. The storyteller includes extra information in this passage that is not included in 1 Kings 8:22–30\. The storyteller says that King Solomon built a bronze platform in the middle of the temple court. The platform was 5 cubits long, 5 cubits wide, and 3 cubits tall. In modern measurements, King Solomon's platform would be 2\.3 meters long, 2\.3 meters wide, and 1\.07 meters tall. A cubit is an ancient measurement that is equal to the length from a person's elbow to the tip of that person's middle finger. King Solomon likely built this platform so that Solomon could speak to all the people more easily and so people could see and hear Solomon better. At this moment, King Solomon stands first and then kneels down on the platform as King Solomon stretches out his hands to heaven and begins to pray.

Stop here and look at an image of King Solomon's temple, including the altar. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at an image of the platform that King Solomon built in the temple courtyard. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon begins when King Solomon declares that Yahweh is the most powerful God in all the earth and in all of heaven. In other words, King Solomon means that no other god that people worship can compare to Yahweh. This is important because other people groups outside of the people of Israel worshipped many gods during King Solomon's time. King Solomon honors Yahweh as the only God that the people of Israel worship.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what kinds of gods do people in your area worship? How do people worship these gods? How do you show that you only worship Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon describes Yahweh as the God who keeps Yahweh's "covenant of love" with the people of Israel. \[The people of Israel are Yahweh's servants who walk in, or obey, Yahweh's ways and commands with their whole heart. In this prayer, King Solomon shows that it is humble and respectful to call yourself someone's servant. This is why King Solomon calls several people Yahweh's servants throughout the prayer.]{.mark} \[Yahweh shows his covenant love to the people of Israel who follow Yahweh]{.mark} and all of Yahweh's commands. In this covenant, both Yahweh and the people of Israel promise to act in a certain way. Yahweh promises to love and protect the people of Israel, and the people of Israel promise to keep Yahweh's commands and to walk the path where Yahweh leads. To walk the path of Yahweh means to obey Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what types of agreements or covenants do you have? What types of covenants do leaders make with their people? Think about your family structure and community structure. How do people agree and then hold each other accountable to the agreements? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon again declares that Yahweh has kept the promises that Yahweh made to King David. In this moment, King Solomon means how Yahweh fulfilled his promise to David in Solomon's time. Yahweh has chosen King Solomon as the next king after King David, and Yahweh has allowed King Solomon to build the temple.

After King Solomon speaks of Yahweh's faithfulness, King Solomon asks Yahweh to continue to be faithful in future generations. King Solomon asks Yahweh to once again keep a covenant that Yahweh made with King David. King Solomon quotes Yahweh's words when King Solomon says that Yahweh promised King David that the people of Israel would always have a king on the throne of Israel. But David's descendants must obey Yahweh as David did. After King Solomon speaks about the original covenant, King Solomon asks Yahweh to be faithful \[to continue to keep]{.mark} the covenant and the words that Yahweh spoke to King David.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how important are words and verbal agreements in your contracts or pledges to other people? Think of a time when you wanted to encourage a trustworthy person to keep a promise they made to another person. How did you help this person continue to keep their promises? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then prays that Yahweh will pay attention to the prayers that the people of Israel will pray. King Solomon asks Yahweh if Yahweh would live on earth with humans, even though the heavens cannot contain the power of Yahweh. Heavens can mean the sky, where Yahweh lives, or both things! King Solomon says that even the grand temple that King Solomon has built for Yahweh is still too small for such a powerful God! King Solomon knows that the temple cannot contain Yahweh, and King Solomon continues to explain what King Solomon means in this prayer.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, where do people believe that gods live? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon does not expect Yahweh to contain himself in the temple. Instead, King Solomon describes what King Solomon hopes Yahweh will do. King Solomon desires for Yahweh to hear King Solomon's prayer to give King Solomon mercy. King Solomon simply wants Yahweh to hear King Solomon and to give Yahweh's attention to King Solomon. In this case, King Solomon is likely not praying a prayer only for himself. Instead, King Solomon is likely asking Yahweh to listen to King Solomon now and in the future, because King Solomon is going to pray for the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you show Yahweh's ability to be both God over all things and also a God who listens to your prayers? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to pay attention to what is happening. In other words, King Solomon wants Yahweh to pay attention to the prayers of Yahweh's people at all times. King Solomon then refers to when Yahweh said that people would worship Yahweh's Name in one place. This is the moment that King Solomon shows what King Solomon is actually praying for. King Solomon does not expect Yahweh to contain himself in the temple, but King Solomon does want Yahweh's Name present in the temple. In biblical times, someone's name showed who that person was, so King Solomon wants the people of Israel to only worship Yahweh in the temple.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what types of places do people go to when they worship deities? How do people interact with deities in these places?

Defining the Scenes
-------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:12–21 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

**In the first scene:** King Solomon faces the altar to pray to Yahweh.

**In the second scene:** The storyteller pauses the story to describe the platform King Solomon built earlier and stands on now to pray.

**In the third scene:** King Solomon prays to Yahweh.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* People of Israel
* King David
* Yahweh
* And platform builders

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

This passage shows a portion of King Solomon's longer prayer as Solomon dedicates the temple to Yahweh. Most of the characters in the story either watch King Solomon pray, or King Solomon speaks about these people or to them. It is good for you to still have the characters present and to show who King Solomon prays to and who King Solomon refers to throughout the passage.

In the first scene, King Solomon prepares to pray to Yahweh. King Solomon faces the altar in the court outside the courtyard of the temple. The assembly of Israel, or that special group of Israelites who have come together for this important purpose, likely stands behind King Solomon.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how do you show action or show specific ways that a person stands or moves? For example, how can you make sure the listener understands that the people were behind King Solomon? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, the storyteller says that King Solomon had built a platform. This means that the storyteller is telling us about something that has already happened. This section gives context and can help us understand how the temple looked. The temple builders, under King Solomon's supervision, built the platform 5 cubits long, 5 cubits wide, and 3 cubits tall. In modern measurements, the builders built the platform 2\.3 meters long, 2\.3 meters wide, and 1\.07 meters tall.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, when you tell a story, how do you talk about the way someone made an item that a person uses in the story? When would you choose to tell the story of how someone made the item? How can you best translate this part of the passage? Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, King Solomon begins to pray and thank Yahweh. King Solomon recognizes that Yahweh is the God above all other gods when King Solomon says that there is no other god in the highest part of heaven or the lowest place under the earth or on earth that compares to Yahweh. In other words, King Solomon says that Yahweh is the greatest god of all gods anywhere. King Solomon then shows Yahweh as a personal and present God when King Solomon shows that Yahweh makes covenants with Yahweh's people and loyally loves his people, the Israelites. King Solomon also says that the people of Israel keep Yahweh's commands with all their heart. When someone does something "with all their heart," that person does that thing happily and well.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: King Solomon has changed from talking about Yahweh to talking to Yahweh. How will you make it clear that King Solomon is talking to Yahweh here? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon recognizes that Yahweh kept Yahweh's earlier covenant with King David when Yahweh chose King Solomon to be king and allowed King Solomon to build the temple. Solomon says that Yahweh said the promise with Yahweh's mouth, and Yahweh kept Yahweh's promise with his hand, or with Yahweh's power. King Solomon is saying that the Israelites can see that Yahweh kept his promise because Yahweh has made King Solomon, David's son, king of Israel, and King Solomon has built the house for Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you translate that Yahweh said a promise with Yahweh's mouth and kept the promise with Yahweh's hand, or power? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon now asks Yahweh to keep another specific covenant that Yahweh made with King David. King Solomon quotes Yahweh when King Solomon refers to how Yahweh promised King David that Yahweh would continue to give the people of Israel a king from King David's family line as long as David's descendants followed Yahweh's commands, just as King David did. King Solomon wants Yahweh to continue this covenant with King Solomon.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: This section has a quote from Yahweh inside King Solomon's prayer. In your language, how can you translate this to show when Solomon speaks his own words and when Solomon quotes Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers of King Solomon and Yahweh's people. First, King Solomon asks this question: "Will God really live on earth? The heavens cannot hold you, and neither can this temple!" Solomon means that Solomon does not believe that Yahweh is supposed to live only in the temple on earth. King Solomon understands that if heaven cannot contain Yahweh, a temple that people built cannot contain Yahweh either. King Solomon is asking a question that he does not expect Yahweh to answer. Instead, Solomon is praising Yahweh for being so great that Yahweh cannot live in one place.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: How will you translate this section to show that King Solomon believes that Yahweh can live anywhere, and no one place is the only place Yahweh lives? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon begs Yahweh to respond to the prayers that King Solomon and the people of Israel pray now and will pray in the future. King Solomon asks Yahweh to open Yahweh's eyes and to give full attention to Yahweh's people's prayers and to what happens in the temple during the day and the night, or all the time. To open your eyes to something means to pay attention and watch what happens, just as a person with their eyes open can see and pay attention to something.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how do you speak about the way that someone pays attention to something or someone? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear and listen to King Solomon and the people of Israel when they pray anytime during the day or night. King Solomon again quotes Yahweh when King Solomon says that Yahweh once promised that Yahweh's "Name would be there" in one place for people to worship Yahweh. King Solomon probably wants to show that Yahweh promises to be present in the temple to meet with the people. King Solomon finishes this part of the prayer when Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the supplications of Yahweh's people when they pray in the temple. Supplication is a way that people can pray to Yahweh. In this case, the people are strongly asking Yahweh to do something for the people.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how do you strongly ask God to do something for you? Pause this audio here.

You will notice that King Solomon speaks about himself in this section as if Solomon were speaking about someone else. King Solomon calls himself Yahweh's "servant."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How will you show that Solomon is talking about himself when Solomon refers to Yahweh's servant? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to forgive the people of Israel when Yahweh hears the prayers that the people pray "towards this place," the temple. If the Israelites were not near the temple, the Israelites could face the direction of the temple to pray, to show that the Israelites were praying to Yahweh. King Solomon expects that Yahweh will hear these prayers and Yahweh will forgive his people of their disobedience. Yahweh will answer these prayers from heaven, the place where Yahweh lives.

* I hope Yahweh continues to be trustworthy! or
* I wonder if Yahweh is hearing my prayers! or
* I feel nervous that Yahweh will change his mind!

> Continue the drama.

King Solomon again recognizes how big and powerful Yahweh is. King Solomon asks, "But, will God really dwell on earth with humans?" King Solomon recognizes that heaven cannot contain Yahweh's power, and the temple is not supposed to contain Yahweh either. Instead, King Solomon asks Yahweh's Name to rest in the temple, as Yahweh promised in another covenant to Moses. King Solomon asks Yahweh to open Yahweh's eyes to all that happens in the temple, both day and night. King Solomon desires for Yahweh to hear the prayers that both King Solomon and the people of Israel will pray in the temple. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the pleas of the people and to forgive the people of Israel when Yahweh hears the people's prayers.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* Solomon is right! Nothing can contain me! or
* I am honored to have my Name in the temple! or
* I will hear the people's prayers!

Filling the Gaps
----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:12–21 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Solomon turns away from the **assembly** of **Israel** and faces the **altar** of Yahweh. In the temple, the altar is a large structure where priests make burnt animal sacrifices. King Solomon stretches out his hands to heaven and prays to **Yahweh**. Heaven is the place where Yahweh lives with his angels. Use the same words or phrases for assembly, altar, Yahweh, Israelites, and Israel as you have in previous passages. For more information, refer to these words in the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **heaven**. Look up heaven in the Master Glossary for more information. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon stands and then kneels down on a bronze platform that stands 5 **cubits** long, 5 cubits wide, and 3 cubits tall. This equals about 2\.3 meters long, 2\.3 meters wide, and 1\.07 meters tall. A person can measure a cubit by measuring the distance between their elbow and the tip of their middle finger. Each cubit is about 44 to 53 centimeters long. Use the same word or phrase for cubits as you used in previous passages. For more information on cubits, refer to the Master Glossary.

Solomon says that Yahweh, the **God** of Israel, kept his **covenant** of **steadfast love** with Yahweh's **servants**, who are Solomon, David, and the Israelites. This covenant is a commitment that requires both people to keep promises to each other. Yahweh's servants keep this covenant with all their **hearts**. Use the same words or phrases for God, covenant, steadfast love, heart, and servants as you have used in previous passages. God, covenant, steadfast love, heart, and servant are in the Master Glossary.

King Solomon reminds Yahweh that Yahweh had promised that there would be a descendant of David on the **throne** of Israel forever if the Israelites follow Yahweh's laws. Yahweh's laws are the instructions that Yahweh gives his people to follow. Use the same word or phrase for throne as you have used in previous passages.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **descendants** and **law**. Descendants and law are in the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon recognizes that King Solomon's **temple** cannot contain Yahweh! King Solomon knows that Yahweh's **Name** is the most important part of the temple. Use the same words or phrases for temple and the Name of Yahweh as you have used in previous passages. Temple is in the Master Glossary.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers and supplications of the people of Israel. When someone prays, that person is talking to God. Supplication is a type of prayer when people ask humbly, but very strongly, for Yahweh to hear them and answer them.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **supplication** and **pray**. Look up prayer in the Master Glossary for more information about the different types of prayers to Yahweh. If you have already translated these types of prayers in another book of the Bible, you may be able to use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks that Yahweh hear the people's prayers and then forgive the people. When Yahweh forgives people, Yahweh has mercy on those people and does not punish them as they deserve.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **forgive**. Forgive is in the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
