## 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 (id: eng-2ch-p11-v1)

Hear and Heart
--------------

In this step, hear 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

This passage is very similar to the passage you may have already translated for 1 Kings 8:31–53\. If you have already translated this passage, listen to your translation of 1 Kings 8:31–53\.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, King Solomon continues the prayer to Yahweh that Solomon began to pray in the previous passage. In this section, King Solomon makes seven requests to Yahweh. King Solomon mostly talks to Yahweh about the whole nation of Israel. In each request, King Solomon gives examples of what may happen, and then King Solomon asks Yahweh to respond in a certain way.

First, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about oaths or promises that people might make to one another because one person has done something wrong to someone else. In this case, both people must stand before the altar in front of the temple and allow Yahweh to judge who is telling the truth. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear both people's arguments and then punish the guilty person and show who is innocent.

Stop here and look at an image of the temple and an image of the altar in the temple courtyard. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people decide who is telling the truth and who is lying? How do people decide if someone is guilty or innocent? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon knows how the people of Israel have disobeyed Yahweh before, and Yahweh has allowed enemy armies to conquer the people. In Solomon's second request, King Solomon asks Yahweh for something in the future. Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people of Israel when the people repent and turn back to Yahweh after an enemy army defeats the people of Israel because they disobeyed. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear from heaven and listen to the people's prayers in the temple.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think of a time when you prayed for a situation that had not happened yet. What did you pray, and why? Pause this audio here.

In King Solomon's third request, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about drought. Drought can happen when there is no rain for a long period of time. Again, King Solomon seems to expect that drought will happen, and King Solomon also recognizes that Yahweh may bring the drought because of the people's sins. King Solomon asks Yahweh to listen and respond to the people of Israel when the people of Israel realize that they have sinned and turn back to Yahweh and pray. King Solomon prays that Yahweh would forgive the people of Israel. Then King Solomon asks that Yahweh would teach the people of Israel how to live in the right way. Finally, King Solomon asks that Yahweh would end the drought and send rain on the land that Yahweh promised to the people of Israel as their inheritance.

Stop here and look at an image of the effects of drought. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at an image of land that is flourishing from rain. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think about a time when your land had no rain for a long time. What happened to the plants? What happened to the animals and people? How did you feel and respond? Pause this audio here.

In King Solomon's fourth request, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about any kind of disaster in the land. First, King Solomon talks about famine and "plague" or terrible sickness. Famine means that people have no food. Terrible sickness means that people have diseases, and that the diseases have spread to many people. King Solomon then lists specific events that could happen, such as hot and dry winds, moisture that rots crops, locusts or grasshoppers, and people who attack from another country. Locusts and grasshoppers are both insects that can easily destroy crops when they eat the crops quickly. A siege happens when an enemy surrounds a city and prevents the people in the city from trading or receiving any supplies or food. In time, the people in the city would have no choice but to leave their city and fight. Again, King Solomon knows the typical problems that Solomon's people will have.

Stop here and look at an image of a blighted plant. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at an image of a plant with mildew. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at images of grasshoppers and locusts. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Think about your community's history and even your family's history. Talk about a time when you or your community experienced a terrible sickness or drought. Share your experiences with the group. Pause this audio here.

The people of Israel must recognize the suffering they have "in their hearts" and turn to Yahweh. King Solomon says that the people will spread their hands to the temple to show that the people know that God, who lives in the temple among the people of Israel, is the source of the people's help. The people must pray and strongly ask for Yahweh's forgiveness. King Solomon then simply asks Yahweh to do two things: forgive and act. King Solomon recognizes that only Yahweh knows every person's motives and attitudes, and King Solomon asks Yahweh to choose how to respond to each person. King Solomon asks Yahweh to remind each person who Yahweh is and that they should honor Yahweh for as long as the people live in Yahweh's land that Yahweh has given to the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How do you normally pray in your culture? What kinds of things do you normally pray for? Pause this audio here.

In King Solomon's fifth request, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about foreigners who are not Israelites but who hear and believe in Yahweh. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the foreigner's prayers, because the foreigner has heard people speak about Yahweh's power and strength. King Solomon then boldly asks Yahweh to do whatever the foreigner asks. King Solomon believes that the foreigner can tell all people about the character of the God of Israel, so that all people, not just the Israelites, will fear Yahweh. Lastly, King Solomon wants all people to know that the temple bears Yahweh's name and Yahweh's name alone. Then people will know that the temple is the place where God is present and that they should worship God there.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think about a time when you prayed for or were kind to foreigners who used to be your enemies. Share your story with the group. Pause this audio here.

In King Solomon's sixth request, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh and asks Yahweh to give victory to the people of Israel when Yahweh tells the people to fight a war with enemies. King Solomon describes to Yahweh that the people will look toward the city that Yahweh has chosen for the people of Israel. The people will also look toward where the temple is as the people pray. When this happens, King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people's prayers and supplications, to make the Israelites strong, and to cause the Israelites to defeat their enemies.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people do with their bodies when they pray? Pause this audio here.

Finally, King Solomon talks about the times when the Israelites will sin \[and when enemy armies will force the Israelites to leave their own land and be slaves in a foreign land.]{.mark} Even though Yahweh is angry when the Israelites sin, King Solomon asks Yahweh to listen to the Israelites' prayer when they turn back to Yahweh and obey him. The Israelites must confess that they have sinned and decide to change before Yahweh will forgive the Israelites and save them.

Defining the Scenes
-------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has seven scenes. Even though King Solomon is praying during the whole passage, it may be easier to act out Solomon's separate requests as separate scenes.

**In the first scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to judge people when one person accuses another person of doing something wrong.

**In the second scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to save the Israelites from their enemies, to return the Israelites to the land Yahweh gave them, and to forgive the Israelites when they pray and turn back to Yahweh.

**In the third scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to forgive the Israelites when they pray and to send rain to end the drought.

**In the fourth scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to forgive the Israelites when they pray and to stop disease and disaster from happening.

**In the fifth scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear foreigners when they pray to Yahweh.

**In the sixth scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to give the Israelites victory when Yahweh sends the Israelites to fight enemies.

**In the seventh scene:** King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear and forgive the Israelites when they pray and to release them from captivity by their enemies.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* People of Israel—this group can act out any part of the drama with people of Israel
* Two people at the altar
* Enemies of Israel—this group can act out any part of the drama with enemies
* Foreigners
* All peoples of the earth
* The Israelites' ancestors
* And Moses

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, each scene represents a different part of King Solomon's prayer to Yahweh. Each scene seems to act as a shorter prayer within the larger prayer. King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about seven situations that will probably happen in Israel. These situations are things that Yahweh has talked about before. Yahweh has promised that Yahweh will act in the way that Solomon asks Yahweh to now. Just like the beginning of this prayer, Solomon asks Yahweh to do what Yahweh promised. King Solomon also asks Yahweh to show mercy on the people of Israel when they repent.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you pray for things or situations that might happen in the future? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon seems to use a pattern when he prays. King Solomon recognizes that something will happen. King Solomon then mentions whether or not the people's sins have caused the thing to happen. King Solomon says that the people must be sorry and ask for Yahweh's forgiveness. Solomon asks that Yahweh hear the people and forgive the people. Lastly, Solomon asks that Yahweh give something to the people in a specific way. This is a common pattern for most scenes.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think back through each section and notice the pattern. Notice how King Solomon uses a lot of the same phrases throughout the prayer. How can you show this pattern in your translation? You will probably want to translate these phrases in the same way throughout the prayer. Pause this audio here.

In the first scene, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about what to do if someone accuses a neighbor of doing something against the person. In this situation, a neighbor can mean a friend or any other person. King Solomon says that both people will stand in front of the altar in the temple courtyard and take an oath, or a strong promise, that they are innocent. King Solomon then asks Yahweh to judge who is telling the truth. King Solomon asks Yahweh to punish the person who does something wrong and to also clear the innocent person of any judgment.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people talk when those people want to emphasize that they are telling the truth? What kinds of words or phrases do you have that might be the same as what King Solomon uses for "oath" in this passage? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about when the Israelites sin and when Yahweh allows enemies to defeat the Israelites. King Solomon uses the word "when," which means that King Solomon expects this situation to happen at some point. However, King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear when the Israelites pray and make supplication to Yahweh. You will remember that when people make supplication, people are very sincerely and humbly begging Yahweh to do something for them. King Solomon also asks Yahweh to forgive the Israelites and return the Israelites to the land that Yahweh gave to their ancestors.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how can you describe supplication? Take time to review the words you used in the last passage for how the Israelites talk to Yahweh through supplication and prayer. Discuss which terms you can use in this passage. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about when the Israelites sin and when Yahweh "shuts up the heavens," which means that Yahweh stops rain from falling from the sky.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will translate that Yahweh has "shut up the heavens," or stopped rain from falling from the sky. Pause this audio here.

When there is a drought, it does not rain for a very long time. A drought can make it difficult for people to grow crops and make food. Again, King Solomon recognizes that the people of Israel may sin against Yahweh and cause the drought. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers of the people and to forgive the people. King Solomon also asks Yahweh to teach the people of Israel the right way to act and then to send rain down onto the land that Yahweh gave as an inheritance to the people of Israel. Many years before, Yahweh gave the land of Israel as a gift to the Israelites. This is not the same as an inheritance that a person receives after someone dies. Yahweh provides the land of Israel, this special place, for the Israelites because Yahweh loves and provides for the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How will you describe that Yahweh has given the land to the people of Israel as an inheritance? Pause this audio here.

In the fourth scene, King Solomon begins to list different types of disasters that could happen to the people of Israel. King Solomon says that the people of Israel could experience famine or plague. Famine is when a large part of the population cannot grow crops and has no food. King Solomon lists different ways that this may happen, like blight, mildew, locusts, or grasshoppers, which all destroy plants that people eat. King Solomon also talks about when an enemy besieges or surrounds an Israelite city. Then the people inside would run out of food. King Solomon finishes the list by saying "whatever disaster or disease" and seems to make sure that he is listing every possible disaster. When these disasters happen, the people can pray to Yahweh, just as Yahweh said the people can. The people of Israel must recognize the suffering they "hold in their hearts." This means that the Israelites recognize that they are suffering because they have sinned. Yahweh knows what is "in our hearts," or what we think or feel. The Israelites have sinned. The Israelites must ask God to forgive them and must stop sinning. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers and forgive the people. King Solomon also asks Yahweh to deal with each person so that each person will always "fear," or honor, Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, what words do you have like "fear" that can have different meanings? How can you show that fear means to honor Yahweh in this passage? Pause this audio here.

In the fifth scene, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about foreigners who may hear about Yahweh and travel to where the people of Israel live. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers of the foreigners who believe and pray towards the temple. King Solomon knows that if Yahweh hears a foreigner's prayer and answers the prayer, the people of Israel and all people will see what Yahweh does and how Yahweh answers, and will know who Yahweh is and fear Yahweh. King Solomon wants everyone to know that the temple only exists for people to honor and praise Yahweh's name. When King Solomon talks about Yahweh's strength and power, Solomon says that Yahweh's name is great, Yahweh has a mighty hand, and Yahweh has an outstretched arm. This means that Yahweh is strong and powerful and deserves the highest honor.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In this passage, King Solomon says that the temple exists for Yahweh's name. In your culture, how do names show the character and reputation of a person? How can you translate this passage to show why Yahweh's name and reputation were important in the temple? How will you translate that Yahweh has a mighty hand and outstretched arm, or that Yahweh has great power? Pause this audio here.

In the sixth scene, King Solomon asks Yahweh to give the people of Israel victory when Yahweh sends the people of Israel to fight against other nations. The people of Israel must turn in the direction of the city where Yahweh is, and the people must pray towards the temple. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers and pleas and to cause the Israelites to win!

In the seventh scene, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about captivity. King Solomon recognizes that the people of Israel will sin. King Solomon also says that Yahweh will allow other nations to capture the people of Israel and keep them in captivity. This is the punishment that Yahweh promised if the Israelites continued to sin against Yahweh. However, King Solomon asks Yahweh to see and hear when the people of Israel turn back to Yahweh with their heart and soul and pray for Yahweh's forgiveness. King Solomon uses the words "sin," "wrong," and "evil" to show how much they realize that they have acted in horrible ways against Yahweh. King Solomon knows that the people must show that they need forgiveness and must ask Yahweh with sincere prayers to forgive them.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text
------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has seven scenes. Even though King Solomon prays a prayer for the whole passage, it may be easier to act out the separate requests as separate scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* People of Israel—this group can act out any part of the drama with people of Israel
* Two people at the altar
* Enemies of Israel—this group can act out any part of the drama with enemies
* Foreigners
* All peoples of the earth
* The Israelites' ancestors
* And Moses

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

First, King Solomon prays to Yahweh about oaths that people swear when they disagree. King Solomon says that when a person brings harm to another person, the two people stand in front of the temple altar and make an oath and promise that they have not done a harmful act. King Solomon then asks Yahweh to judge the two people and to condemn the guilty person and show the innocence of the person who has not done a harmful act.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing the guilty person, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I am afraid of what Yahweh will do! or
* I feel anxious that everyone will know what I did! or
* I should not have done this sin!

> Continue the drama.

Second, King Solomon prays to Yahweh about when the Israelites sin and when Yahweh allows enemies to defeat the Israelites. When the Israelites turn back to Yahweh and praise Yahweh sincerely, King Solomon asks that Yahweh listen. Then Yahweh can forgive the people and bring the people of Israel back to the land that Yahweh promised to the people of Israel.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing King Solomon, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* Please hear my prayer, Yahweh! or
* I have faith that Yahweh will hear me! or
* I hope the people of Israel remember this prayer.

> Continue the drama.

Third, King Solomon prays to Yahweh about drought in the land. King Solomon knows that Yahweh can make the rain stop when the people of Israel do not follow Yahweh. When drought happens in this way, King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people of Israel when the people pray to Yahweh and no longer sin. King Solomon also asks Yahweh to teach the people the right way to live and to send rain down on the land that Yahweh gave to the people of Israel as an inheritance.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I am sad when my people sin against me! or
* King Solomon is very wise; or
* I want to listen to my people when they pray.

> Continue the drama.

Fourth, King Solomon prays to Yahweh about famine and plagues. King Solomon recognizes the different ways that famine can happen. King Solomon knows that the people of Israel will sin and that Yahweh will then allow blights, mildew, locusts, and grasshoppers to destroy their crops and enemies to besiege their cities. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people when they are in the middle of any disaster or disease and begin to pray. King Solomon asks Yahweh to see the people as they spread their hands towards the temple and pray to Yahweh for forgiveness. King Solomon then asks Yahweh to forgive the people and to deal with each person because of what they think in their hearts. Yahweh knows what people think and how to treat each person so that each person will always fear and honor Yahweh.

Pause the drama. Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" A person might answer things like:

* We are going to lose all of our crops! or
* I am scared of what is going to happen next! or
* Why is this happening to us?

> Continue the drama.

Fifth, King Solomon prays to Yahweh about how to treat foreigners who travel to Israel because they have heard about Yahweh. King Solomon recognizes that the foreigners will likely arrive because the foreigners have learned about Yahweh's great name, mighty hand, and outstretched arm! King Solomon then asks that Yahweh would hear the foreigner's prayer and give the foreigner whatever they ask for. King Solomon believes that all people will see what Yahweh does, will honor Yahweh, and will know that people honor Yahweh in the temple.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing the foreigner, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I am so grateful to know Yahweh! or
* I trust that Yahweh will answer! or
* I must tell other people about Yahweh!

Continue the drama.

Sixth, King Solomon prays to Yahweh for victory for the people of Israel when Yahweh sends the Israelites to fight with their enemies in different places. King Solomon asks Yahweh to cause the Israelites to win when the people pray towards the city and temple.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* We need Yahweh's help! or
* We must remember to pray to ask Yahweh for help; or
* I feel afraid to go to war!

Continue the drama.

Seventh, King Solomon speaks to Yahweh about possible captivity in the future. King Solomon realizes that the people of Israel may sin against Yahweh, and then enemies may capture the people. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people as they pray from the different lands and ask for forgiveness. King Solomon asks Yahweh to forgive the people.

Filling the Gaps
----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:22–39 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

King Solomon begins to pray for neighbors, or people, who must take oaths before the **altar** in the **temple**. When two people disagree, those people must stand before the altar and take an oath or a strong promise to say that they are innocent. For more information on altar and temple, refer to the Master Glossary, and use the same words or phrases as you have in previous passages.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **oath** and **neighbor**. In this case, a neighbor can mean any person you interact with. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about oath and neighbor. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear from **heaven,** where Yahweh lives, then **judge** Yahweh's **servants** and condemn the guilty person and vindicate the innocent person. In this passage, a servant is someone who is devoted to Yahweh. You will remember that when someone judges another person, they decide if that person is guilty or innocent. To condemn a person means to punish a person. To vindicate means to say that someone is innocent. For more information on heaven, judge, and servants, refer to the Master Glossary, and use the same words or phrases as you have in previous passages.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **guilty**. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about guilty. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then speaks to Yahweh about future moments when the people of **Israel** might sin against Yahweh and another army defeats the Israelites. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people when they **pray** for **forgiveness** and **praise** or thank Yahweh. King Solomon says that the people will pray in **supplication** in the temple. You will remember that supplication means to pray sincerely and humbly. In other words, the people of Israel need to show that they mean what they are praying. Then King Solomon asks Yahweh to forgive the people's sins. Sin is when a person does anything that goes against what Yahweh asks them to do. Use the same words or phrases for Israel, pray, forgive, supplication, and praise as you did in previous passages. Look up Israel, pray, forgive, and praise in the Master Glossary for more information.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **sin**. Look up sin in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then says that Yahweh shuts up the heavens so that it does not rain\*\*,\*\* which means that Yahweh brings drought. King Solomon talks about "heavens" to mean the sky from which rain falls, and not the place where Yahweh lives.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **heaven**. If you have already translated heaven to mean "sky" in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Look up heaven in the Master Glossary for more information. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the prayers of the people and to send rain to the land that Yahweh gave to the people of Israel as their inheritance. In this passage, King Solomon also says that Yahweh calls the Israelites his inheritance, or treasure. This means that the land belongs to the Israelites because Yahweh has given it to them, and that the people of Israel belong to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **inheritance**. If you have already translated this idea in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then speaks to Yahweh about famine and plague. Famine happens when people experience a widespread loss of crops and food. Plague happens when diseases, illnesses, or disasters spread to many people. King Solomon also lists other things that cause famine, such as blight, mildew, grasshoppers, locusts, and a siege on a city. Blight is when hot and dry winds blow and destroy crops. Mildew is when plants become too damp and rot. To besiege a city means that people from another land surround a city so that people cannot leave the city or receive supplies from outside the city walls.

Stop here and look at the photos again of a land that has experienced blight or mildew. Look at photos of grasshoppers and locusts. Discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **famine**, **plague**, **disease**, **blight**, **mildew**, **grasshoppers**, **locusts**, and **siege**. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about siege. If you have already translated these words in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh knows people's **hearts**, and Yahweh wants everyone to fear Yahweh. You will remember that a person's heart is the way that people in the Bible talked about where a person's thoughts, feelings, and decisions happen. When someone fears Yahweh, that person honors and respects Yahweh very much. Use the same word or phrase for heart as you have used previously, and refer to heart in the Master Glossary for more information.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will translate that people should **fear** Yahweh. For more information, refer to "fear of God" in the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon wants Yahweh to protect the land that Yahweh gave to the **ancestors** of the people of Israel. Ancestors are people in a person's family who are older than that person or lived before that person. Use the same word or phrase for ancestors as you used in previous passages.

King Solomon then speaks to Yahweh about the foreigner who might hear about Yahweh and travel to where the people of Israel live. King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the foreigner when the foreigner prays towards the temple. Solomon talks about foreigners who do not live in the land of Israel, but come from far away just to pray to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **foreigner**, when it means a person who does not regularly live in the land. Look up foreigner in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon then speaks to Yahweh about the people of Israel going to war. King Solomon asks **Yahweh** to bring victory to the people of Israel when they pray to Yahweh in the city and temple that honors Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. Look up Yahweh in the Master Glossary for more information.

King Solomon then prays to Yahweh about captivity. King Solomon again knows that the people will likely sin and that captors, or enemies who capture the people, will take the people and hold them captive in another land. When someone holds someone captive, they force that person to stay in one place.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **captive** and **captor**. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the people when they repent or turn away from their sins and return to follow Yahweh. The people stop acting in wrong and wicked ways.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **repent** and **wicked**. Look up repent and wicked in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated these words in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon says that the people turn back to Yahweh with their "**heart and soul**," which means they show that they are completely devoted to Yahweh. Use the same words or phrases for "heart and soul" as you used in 1 Kings 2:4, and refer to the Master Glossary for more information about soul.

## 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 (id: eng-2ch-p12-v1)

Hear and Heart
--------------

In this step, hear 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, King Solomon finishes praying to Yahweh for Yahweh's blessing. It is important to remember that this prayer is a part of a longer series of prayers that King Solomon has prayed. King Solomon has just built the temple for Yahweh and for people who worship Yahweh. Yahweh promised King Solomon's father, King David, that King Solomon would become king and would build the temple. Yahweh has fulfilled Yahweh's promises.

Stop and look at a photo or illustration of King Solomon's temple as a group. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon has completed the temple and asks Yahweh to show favor and for Yahweh's presence to permanently live in the temple. It is important to remember that in previous passages, the Israelites brought the ark of the covenant to the temple. King Solomon commanded the people to bring the ark because King Solomon knew that the ark represented the presence of Yahweh. King Solomon can now pray for Yahweh's presence and blessing over the temple.

Stop and, as a group, look at a photo or illustration of the ark of the covenant. Pause this audio here.

Stop and look at a diagram of Solomon's temple, including the inner sanctuary and holy rooms. Pause this audio here.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: Think of a time when you finished a huge task or a process that took a long time. How did you feel once you completed it? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to open his eyes and ears to every prayer that people will offer in the temple. King Solomon is asking Yahweh to be aware and to watch and listen to the prayers of Yahweh's people.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: Describe the emotions you feel when you want something important to happen. Think of the thoughts and feelings you have and share with the group. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to arise, or act, and come rest, or live, in the temple. This means that Yahweh will be present forever in the temple. King Solomon also says Yahweh should come with the ark of the covenant. King Solomon recognizes that the ark of the covenant represents where Yahweh has lived among his people. It is important to remember that Yahweh's presence was with the ark and brought victory to Israel. Both the temple and the ark show that Yahweh is with the Israelites. King Solomon says that the ark represents Yahweh's strength or power.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: Think of a time when you prayed and asked God to fix a problem in your life or to answer your prayer. What happened after you prayed? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon prays for Yahweh to bless the priests by "clothing them in salvation." King Solomon is actually asking for Yahweh's blessing and salvation to cover or be with the priests like clothing. The priests experience Yahweh's salvation and show how Yahweh saves the people. The priests have important responsibilities in the temple, and the priests need Yahweh to help them do all of their duties. King Solomon continues by praying in hope that the people of Israel who are faithful and loyal to Yahweh will rejoice and worship Yahweh because of Yahweh's goodness to the people.

Stop here and look at a photo of what a priest would normally wear. Pause this audio here.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: Imagine that a king or the highest leader in your community prayed for you or honored you in front of the entire community. How would you react or feel? Pause this audio here.

In the last section of the prayer, King Solomon prays for himself. King Solomon asks Yahweh not to reject King Solomon. King Solomon is likely asking Yahweh humbly to bless King Solomon and to show King Solomon favor as King Solomon leads the people of Israel. Yahweh has anointed or set apart King Solomon to lead the people of Israel. In this moment, King Solomon asks for blessings for himself and the future kings of Israel. King Solomon then mentions King David and Yahweh's blessing on King David. As King David's son, King Solomon knows that Yahweh has blessed King David, and King Solomon asks for Yahweh to give the same steadfast, or faithful love, to King Solomon.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you remember your ancestors or other important people in your life? Think of a time when you felt the same blessings in life that your ancestors also felt. Share your experience with the group. Pause this audio here.

After King Solomon finishes his prayer, Yahweh responds. Yahweh sends down fire from heaven, or the sky, to the altar. The fire completely burns up the sacrifices that people offered when they moved the ark of the covenant, as well as the burnt offerings for the temple. Yahweh sends fire and his glory to show that Yahweh accepts and approves of both the temple and the sacrifices that King Solomon, the priests, and the people offered. Yahweh also shows his power when Yahweh sends the fire!

Show a photo or illustration of fire coming down from heaven to the altar. Pause this audio here.

It is important to remember that the temple included outdoor spaces as well, because most people could only go to certain parts of the temple. Only priests and the high priest could go inside the inner courtyard and the holy places. King Solomon likely prays in the outer courtyards before anyone enters the temple area.

Stop and review the diagram of Solomon's temple, including the inner courtyard and holy rooms as well as the outdoor spaces. Pause this audio here.

When Yahweh's glory fills the temple, the priests cannot enter the temple because there is no space. The priests are not afraid or unwilling to go in, but Yahweh's glory fills the temple completely, and the priests cannot go in. The priests and the people see Yahweh accept the sacrifices and offerings, and Yahweh's glory above the temple. The people of Israel bow down to honor and worship Yahweh.

Stop and look at a photo of people kneeling or bowing to the ground. Pause this audio here.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people show respect for a person in authority? For example, in some cultures, people bow. In other cultures, people may clap their hands. Discuss as a group how your culture might respond. Pause this audio here.

The people of Israel begin to worship Yahweh and to offer praise to Yahweh. The people of Israel respond to Yahweh's presence by saying, "He is good; His steadfast love continues forever." The people of Israel often respond like this to Yahweh's goodness, faithfulness, and steadfast love. The priests also sang this in earlier passages.

Defining the Scenes
-------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

**In the first scene:** King Solomon prays for Yahweh to hear the Israelites' prayers and take care of the Israelites.

**In the second scene:** Yahweh sends down fire to accept the sacrifices and burnt offerings, and Yahweh's glory fills the temple. The priests see Yahweh's glory and cannot enter the temple.

**In the third scene:** The people of Israel see the fire and the glory above the temple, so the people bow down and worship Yahweh.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* Priests
* People of Israel
* And King David

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, King Solomon finishes his series of prayers when Solomon asks Yahweh to hear the Israelites' prayers and take care of the Israelites. Solomon uses a word to start his prayer that shows that Solomon is coming to the end of his prayer and is summarizing what Solomon has been praying for.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how can you show the transition to the end of King Solomon's prayer? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon uses poetic language in his prayer to Yahweh. King Solomon first asks Yahweh to watch and hear what King Solomon is about to pray, and to continue doing this for every prayer that the people of Israel pray in the temple.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how will you describe God seeing or hearing something when you cannot see God? How does your culture describe God as having human experiences like seeing or hearing? How can you translate the poetic language of Solomon's prayer? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon also asks for Yahweh to arise and rest in the temple, along with the ark of the covenant. Yahweh was not sitting, but when King Solomon asks Yahweh to "arise," Solomon is asking Yahweh to act. Yahweh was not sleeping, but when King Solomon asks Yahweh to rest, Solomon is asking Yahweh to be present and live in the temple.

King Solomon then prays that Yahweh would bless and cover the priests in Yahweh's salvation. Solomon compares salvation, or the way Yahweh saves, to a garment that people wear. Just like clothes are with people wherever they go, Solomon asks Yahweh's salvation to be with the priests. The priests can then show Yahweh's salvation to the people, like a person can show what clothes that person wears. King Solomon is asking Yahweh to help the priests carry out the duties that Yahweh has given to the priests. King Solomon then prays that the faithful and loyal people of Israel will praise Yahweh for Yahweh's goodness. It is likely that King Solomon is asking Yahweh to also help the people of Israel to see all of the good that Yahweh has done and will continue to do.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how will you describe Yahweh covering the priests with salvation like a person covers themselves in clothes? Pause this audio here.

King Solomon ends his prayers by asking Yahweh to accept and anoint King Solomon as the King of Israel. You will remember that leaders poured oil over the heads of new kings to show that Yahweh had chosen them to be king. Therefore, storytellers often referred to kings with the phrase "anointed person." King Solomon asks Yahweh to remember Yahweh's steadfast love for King David. Yahweh loved King David, and King Solomon desired for Yahweh to love Solomon in that way too.

In the second scene, Yahweh responds to King Solomon's prayer. Yahweh sends down fire from heaven, or the sky, to burn up the sacrifices and burnt offerings that the people placed on the altar. Yahweh shows that Yahweh approves of the temple that Solomon built. Yahweh's glory fills the entire temple and leaves no room for anything else. It is likely that Yahweh showed Yahweh's presence, or glory, with something people could see or feel, like a bright light or a cloud. Yahweh's glory filled the temple so much that the priests could not enter the temple.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how will you describe the fire from heaven, or the sky? How can you translate Yahweh's glory in this passage? Pause this audio here.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: How can you describe that the priests cannot enter the temple sanctuary because of Yahweh's glory? Discuss possible ways to translate this. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, the people of Israel see Yahweh's fire on the altar, and the people can see Yahweh's presence over the temple. The people of Israel \[responded when they bowed down to the ground and worshipped Yahweh.]{.mark} The people kneeled on the pavement, which was the flat stones that made the floor in the courtyard. The people of Israel said, "He is good; His steadfast love continues forever." In this case, "he" refers to Yahweh, and the people of Israel use this phrase in the same way that they use it in other moments to show how they feel about what Yahweh has done.

Stop here and look at a picture of natural stone similar to the floor in the temple. Pause this audio here.

Stop and discuss this question as a group: Review how you translated the words, "He is good, his love endures forever," in 2 Chronicles 5:13 and translate it the same way you did before. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text
------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

* King Solomon
* Yahweh
* Priests
* People of Israel
* And King David

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses:

After King Solomon built the temple, King Solomon stood before the people of Israel and prayed to Yahweh. King Solomon prayed to Yahweh and asked Yahweh to watch and hear King Solomon's prayers and every prayer that people prayed in the temple.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing King Solomon, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I hope Yahweh answers my prayers! or
* I must take care of the people of Israel!

Ask the people playing the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

* I hope Yahweh hears our prayers; or
* We feel honored that King Solomon is praying for us; or
* Wow! Look at what King Solomon has built for Yahweh!

Continue the drama.

King Solomon then prayed and asked Yahweh to come and fill the temple and to live with the ark of the covenant.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing King Solomon, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I feel worried about what Yahweh will do! or
* The ark of the covenant is finally here! or
* Surely Yahweh will answer!

Continue the drama.

King Solomon also prayed that Yahweh give the priests Yahweh's salvation and blessing.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing a priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I do not want to do anything to upset Yahweh! or
* I must do all I can to bless Yahweh and to help the people of Israel; or
* I am grateful King Solomon is praying for me!

Continue the drama.

After Solomon prayed for the priests, King Solomon prayed for Yahweh's faithful people. King Solomon prayed that the people of Israel would always rejoice because of Yahweh's goodness.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I am happy that King Solomon really wants my blessing! or
* I love that my people are praying to me! or
* I want my people to always remember how good I am to them.

Continue the drama.

King Solomon finished his prayers and asked Yahweh not to reject king Solomon, but instead to remember the love Yahweh showed to David.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing King Solomon, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* I really need Yahweh's blessing! or
* I wish my father could see the temple; or
* I want Yahweh to love me as loyally as Yahweh loved my father, David.

Continue the drama.

After King Solomon finished praying, Yahweh sent fire down from heaven and burned up all of the sacrifices and burnt offerings that people placed on the altar in the temple. Yahweh's glory then completely filled the temple and left no room for anything or anyone else.

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing King Solomon, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* Yahweh has answered my prayers! or
* Yahweh must really approve of the new temple! or
* I feel so grateful for all that Yahweh has done!

Continue the drama.

Yahweh's glory filled the temple so much that the priests could not enter the temple.

Pause the drama. Ask the people playing the priests, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

* How will we perform our duties? or
* Yahweh is here! or
* I am in awe of Yahweh!

Continue the drama.

When the people of Israel saw the fire on the altar and Yahweh's glory over the temple, the people of Israel immediately worshipped Yahweh. The people of Israel bowed all the way to the ground and said, "Yahweh is good. Yahweh's love endures forever."

Pause the drama. Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

* I am overjoyed that Yahweh is here! or
* I must bow because Yahweh is so powerful! or
* I must never doubt that Yahweh will come!

Filling the Gaps
----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 6:40–7:3 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

King Solomon prays to **Yahweh** to listen to the people when the people **pray** in the **temple** that King Solomon built for Yahweh. King Solomon asks Yahweh to see and hear all that King Solomon is praying and to hear and see every prayer that people will pray in the temple. King Solomon specifically says "Yahweh **God**" in this passage when Solomon speaks to Yahweh.

Use the same words or phrases for God, prayer, temple, and Yahweh as you used in previous passages and throughout. For more information on God, pray, Yahweh, or temple, refer to the Master Glossary.

King Solomon prayed for Yahweh to come to the temple and to make the temple Yahweh's resting place. King Solomon also mentions the **ark of the covenant** and asks Yahweh to rest in the temple, much like Yahweh has rested on the ark of the covenant. In this passage, Solomon calls the ark the "ark of Yahweh's strength" rather than the ark of the covenant, because the ark was a symbol of Yahweh's presence and Yahweh's strength. King Solomon wants the temple to be the place that Yahweh fills. For more information on "ark of the covenant," refer to the Master Glossary, and remember that Solomon calls the ark the "ark of Yahweh's strength" in this passage.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **resting place**. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon prayed that Yahweh would clothe the **priests** in salvation. This likely means that King Solomon wants Yahweh to clothe the priests in salvation as the priests serve in the temple. Use the same word or phrase for priests as you used in previous passages and throughout. For more information on priests, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for **salvation**. Look up salvation in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

King Solomon asks Yahweh to make Yahweh's faithful, or godly, people rejoice in Yahweh's goodness. Faithful people are people who are godly, or who continually follow Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will say **faithful**, or **godly**, people. Pause this audio here.

To finish the prayers, King Solomon prays for Yahweh to not reject the anointed one, or person. Anointed one refers to the person who is currently the king that Yahweh has chosen. King Solomon also refers to Yahweh's steadfast love for King David, who is Yahweh's **servant**, and King Solomon prays for Yahweh to love King Solomon in the same way. Use the same word or phrase for servant as you used in previous passages. For more information on servant, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **steadfast love** and **anointed one**. Look up **anoint** in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated these words in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Immediately after King Solomon finishes praying, Yahweh sends down fire from heaven, or the sky, onto the **sacrifices** and **burnt** **offerings** that were on the altar. Yahweh's **glory** then fills the temple. Yahweh's glory fills the temple so much that the priests cannot enter. For more information on heaven, sacrifice, burnt offering, or glory, refer to the Master Glossary, and translate these words in the same way you have translated them in previous passages.

When the **Israelites** see Yahweh's glory over the temple, the people of Israel immediately bow down to the ground to worship Yahweh. Solomon says that Yahweh is good, which means kind, joyful, or pleasing. Use the same word or phrase for Israelites as you have used previously, and refer to Israelites in the Master Glossary for more information.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for **good**, **bow**, or **worship**. Look up bow and worship in the Master Glossary for more information.

Speaking the Word
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
