Setting the Stage
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 36:17–23 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last story, King Zedekiah of Judah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar. Zedekiah and the people of Judah refused to listen to Yahweh's prophets, so Yahweh became angry and decided to judge them.

Yahweh causes King Nebuchadnezzar of the Chaldeans, or Babylonians, to attack Judah. Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers kill Judah's young men in the temple of Yahweh. Nebuchadnezzar shows no compassion for anyone. Instead, Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers kill young men and women, as well as old people and weak people. Yahweh allows all the people of Judah to be in the hand, or the power, of Nebuchadnezzar. So, just like Yahweh said would happen through the prophet Jeremiah, Nebuchadnezzar kills many people in the city of Jerusalem.

Nebuchadnezzar takes all of the valuable items that the people used to serve in the temple and all the temple treasures. The Babylonians also take the treasures of King Zedekiah and his officials to Babylon. The soldiers burn down Yahweh's temple and break down Jerusalem's city walls. The soldiers also burn down all of the palaces, or large houses, and destroy all of the valuable things in the city.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what are the signs that people have abandoned or destroyed a community? Tell a story of a time when someone completely destroyed or abandoned a community. Pause this audio here.

Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers take all the people of Judah who are still alive to Babylon as prisoners. Those prisoners become slaves to Nebuchadnezzar and his descendants until the kingdom of Persia becomes powerful and replaces the kingdom of Babylonia. The Persians would conquer many kingdoms until the Persian Kingdom grew to include territory from India in the east to Ionia in the west.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a map of the Persian Kingdom during the reign of King Cyrus. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh fulfills his message that Jeremiah the prophet had spoken, and the land of Judah lies empty for all the time that the people did not observe the sabbath rest. According to the Law of Moses, the people were not supposed to grow anything in the land every seventh year. But the people of Judah did grow things every year. So the land of Judah lies empty for 70 years to make up for all the years the people did not allow the land to rest.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your community, are there times when people allow the land, animals, or people to rest? What might happen if people never let their land or bodies rest? Pause this audio here.

Jeremiah said that the people of Judah would live in exile for 70 years. Scholars disagree about when the time of exile began and ended. One explanation is that the exile began when Nebuchadnezzar first took people to Babylon and ended with Cyrus' announcement. Another explanation is that the exile began when Nebuchadnezzar destroyed the temple and ended when the Israelites rebuilt the temple. Either way, the Israelites' exile lasted around 70 years.

Around 70 years after Nebuchadnezzar destroys the temple, King Cyrus of Persia takes over the kingdom of Babylon and begins to rule over Babylon. The storyteller gives us hope by saying Yahweh will fulfill Jeremiah's prophecy and allow the people of Judah to return to their land.

In the first year that Cyrus is the king of Persia, Yahweh causes Cyrus to write a message and send it throughout his kingdom. In the Persian Kingdom, royal messengers traveled to different parts of the kingdom to deliver the king's announcements. The royal messengers then read the king's message aloud to the people. King Cyrus's message said: "Yahweh, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. Yahweh has chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem in Judah. May Yahweh your God be with all of you who are his people. You are free to go up to Jerusalem."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone received help or freedom from a person they least expected. Pause this audio here.

In King Cyrus' message, Cyrus recognizes Yahweh as the one who made Cyrus successful. Cyrus gives his blessing, or favor, to the people of Judah to return to their land and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. The story of the return from Babylon to Jerusalem continues in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah.

Defining the Scenes
-------------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 36:17–23 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

**In the first scene:** Yahweh causes King Nebuchadnezzar and his army to attack the city of Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar kills the young men in the temple. Nebuchadnezzar's soldiers do not spare anyone. The soldiers kill the young, the old, and even the weak people.

**In the second scene:** The Babylonian soldiers take all of the valuables from the temple, the king's house, and the houses of his officials. Then the soldiers burn down the temple and other important buildings. The soldiers also destroy the walls that surround Jerusalem. The Babylonians take all the treasure and the remaining people to Babylon as prisoners. The people of Judah arrive in Babylon and begin to serve Nebuchadnezzar and his family as slaves.

**In the third scene:** The people of Judah are slaves for 70 years. During that time, the land of Judah rests, and no one grows anything. King Cyrus becomes the new king of Babylon and Persia after the Persian Kingdom defeats the Babylonians.

**In the fourth scene:** Yahweh causes King Cyrus to send out an official message throughout his land. In the message, Cyrus recognizes Yahweh and gives Cyrus' blessing to the people of Judah to return to their land and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

The characters in this passage are:

* Yahweh
* King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon
* The Babylonian army
* The people of Judah, including the young, old, and weak
* The remnant of the Jewish people who go to Babylon
* Jeremiah
* King Cyrus of Persia
* And King Cyrus' messenger

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

The storyteller introduces events by saying it is Yahweh who caused the king of the Chaldeans to attack Jerusalem. The storyteller is referring to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon. The Chaldeans lived in southern Babylonia. So, "Chaldeans" was another way to say Babylonians.

Nebuchadnezzar allows his soldiers to kill the young men of Judah with their swords inside Yahweh's temple. Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers show no compassion for Judah's people. Instead, the soldiers kill young and old people, men and women, and even those who are sick or weak.

Yahweh gave all the people into Nebuchadnezzar's "hand." In the original language, storytellers used the hand as an image of power. Like a strong hand holding something tightly, the king has control over the people. So, in other words, Yahweh allowed Nebuchadnezzar to have power over the people of Judah.

Nebuchadnezzar has his soldiers take all of the valuable objects from inside the temple, both great and small, to Babylon. In other words, the soldiers take every valuable part of the temple regardless of size. This would have included smaller items like pure gold serving spoons to large, heavy bronze pillars. The soldiers take all the valuables from the temple, the king's palace, and the homes of his officials.

After taking what they want, the soldiers destroy everything else. The soldiers burn down the temple of Yahweh, the king's palace, and all the other important buildings in Jerusalem. The soldiers also break down the stone wall that surrounds Jerusalem, which leaves Jerusalem unprotected.

Nebuchadnezzar takes the remaining people who escaped the sword, or the people whom the soldiers did not kill, to be prisoners in Babylon. The prisoners from Judah become slaves who serve Nebuchadnezzar and his descendants in Babylon.

Stop here and discuss with your group: Tell a story of a time when enemies destroyed a sacred place in your community. Pay attention to what words you use to describe the destruction of the land after the enemies left. Pause this audio here.

The storyteller gives us hope by telling us that the people of Judah will not be slaves in Babylon forever, but only until the king of Persia comes to power.

We know the people of Judah were exiles in Babylon for around 70 years. During this time, the land enjoys its sabbath rest. This means nobody in Israel plants crops during these years, and that this makes up for all the sabbath years when people had previously worked the land. According to Yahweh's law, the people were supposed to let the land rest every seven years, but the people had disobeyed.

The prophet Jeremiah warned the people of Judah that they would be prisoners in Babylon for 70 years. Everything happens just as Yahweh said it would through Jeremiah.

The kingdom of Persia defeats the kingdom of Babylonia, and King Cyrus of Persia begins to rule over Babylon. During King Cyrus's first year as the king over Babylon, Yahweh stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation, or official announcement. In other words, Yahweh causes Cyrus to have the desire to send a message throughout Cyrus' country.

Stop here and discuss with your group: In your language, how do people talk about something or someone motivating a person to do something? What special language do they use? Pause this audio here.

Official messengers go throughout the Persian Kingdom and tell everyone the king's message. King Cyrus says, "Yahweh, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. Yahweh has chosen me to build a temple for Yahweh in Jerusalem in Judah. May Yahweh your God be with all of you who are his people. You are free to go up to Jerusalem."

The exile of Judah comes to an end, and King Cyrus allows the people of Judah to return to their land.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

----------------

Listen to an audio version of 2 Chronicles 36:17–23 in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh brings the **King** of the Babylonians against Jerusalem. A king is someone who rules over a city or territory, like a region or a country. Nebuchadnezzar ruled over the kingdom of Babylonia. Use the same word or phrase for king as you used in previous passages. For more information on king, refer to the Master Glossary.

King Nebuchadnezzar kills the young men of Judah with a sword in the **sanctuary**. The word "sanctuary" means a place that people set apart to worship God. Here, it refers specifically to Yahweh's temple in Jerusalem. Use the same word or phrase for sanctuary as you used in previous passages. For more information on sanctuary, refer to the Master Glossary.

God gives the people of Judah into Nebuchadnezzar's **hand**. The storyteller uses the image of a hand to represent power. So, in other words, Yahweh allowed Nebuchadnezzar to have power over the people of Judah. Use the same word or phrase for "in the hand of" as you used in previous passages.

The soldiers take all of the valuable treasures out of the **temple** of God. **Yahweh** is a name that God gives himself. It reminds people of the covenant Yahweh made with the Israelites. Israelites worship Yahweh in the temple or the "house of God." Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh and temple as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and temple, refer to the Master Glossary.

The soldiers burn down the temple and break down **Jerusalem's** walls. Jerusalem was the capital city of the kingdom of Judah. Use the same word or phrase for Jerusalem as you used in previous passages. For more information on Jerusalem, refer to the Master Glossary.

The soldiers also burn down the palace of King Zedekiah as well as the homes of Zedekiah's officials. Here, palace refers to a big, protected house instead of specifically referring to the king's house.

Stop here and discuss how you will say "big, protected house" in your language. Pause this audio here.

The people of Judah who the soldiers do not kill become the **servants** of Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuchadnezzar's **sons**. Here, a servant refers to someone who does not get paid for his work. This person does not have the freedom to leave his master whenever he wants. In other words, this person is a slave and the property of his master. Nebuchadnezzar's sons refer to his descendants and not just Nebuchadnezzar's biological sons. Use the same words or phrases for servant and sons as you used in previous passages. For more information on servant or sons, refer to the Master Glossary.

The Jewish people in Babylon serve Nebuchadnezzar's family until the **Kingdom** of Persia comes to power. Kingdom refers to a territory that a king rules. Use the same word or phrase for kingdom as you used in previous passages. For more information on kingdom, refer to the Master Glossary.

The land of Judah enjoys its **sabbaths** for 70 years. According to the law of Yahweh, the Israelites needed to let the land rest every seventh year by not growing anything. Just like people set apart the sabbath day for Yahweh, the seventh year of planting belonged to God. By resting every seventh year, the people learned that they could trust God for all that the people needed. It also allowed the land to continue to be productive. But the Israelites did not keep the sabbaths for many years, so God uses the time of the people's exile to allow the land to rest. Use the same word or phrase for sabbath as you used in previous passages. For more information on sabbath, refer to the Master Glossary.

Jeremiah warned the people when he spoke the **word** of Yahweh, but no one listened to him. The word of Yahweh is every word that God tells people. In this case, Yahweh spoke through the words of the prophet Jeremiah. Use the same word or phrase for the "word" as you used in previous passages. For more information on the "word," refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh stirred up the spirit of King Cyrus to let his people return to Jerusalem. "Stirred up the spirit" is special language that means God caused Cyrus to have a strong desire to let the Israelites go. When the Bible uses the word spirit, the focus is on the relationship that a person has with God.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for "**stirred up the spirit**." Look up **spirit** in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

In his official message, Cyrus calls **God** "Yahweh, the God of **heaven**." Yahweh is a name that God gives himself. God is the most powerful spiritual being who created everything. Heaven refers to the place where God lives. Use the same words or phrases for God and heaven as you used in previous passages. For more information on God and heaven, refer to the Master Glossary.

Cyrus wants to see the people rebuild the temple in **Judah**. Judah refers to the southern kingdom of the nation of Israel. Use the same word or phrase for Judah as you used in previous passages. For more information on Judah, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word
-----------------

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest\-to\-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
